analysis.title: Fixed Income Weekly Update, November 2nd, 2026
key_insights: Treasury yields fell for a fourth straight week. The 2-year yield dropped 9.4 bp to 4.59% and the 10-year dropped 6.6 bp to 4.93%, a bull steepening, with 2s/10s at 0.34%.
The week began with upward pressure on yields after weak Treasury auctions and stronger-than-expected durable goods orders. Yields reversed Thursday on easing inflation signals.
The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% and signaled that persistent inflation and solid growth could warrant another hike in December.
Q3 core PCE slowed to 2.5% annualized from 3.3% in Q2, while Q3 GDP grew 3.4%, stronger than expected.
A sharp Friday selloff in technology stocks on AI spending and profitability concerns drove safe-haven demand for Treasuries. The Nasdaq fell 2.9%.
Warsh's cautious comments reduced the implied probability of a December rate hike.
Broadcom's CDS spread has risen from about 40 bp in May to 193 bp, and Nvidia's to about 147 bp. Piper reads this as credit markets doubting the return on AI capital spending.

Bear case for Treasuries: WTI above $104 on Middle East tensions, three Fed officials calling for more tightening (Logan favoring at least 2 more hikes), September PCE re-accelerating, and strong Q3 GDP and consumer spending.

Bull case for Treasuries: Middle East tensions and the November 3 elections supporting safe-haven demand, further equity weakness, an ECB hold with a growth warning, S&P's negative outlook on Meta, and a slower Q3 employment cost index.

Week ahead is led by the U.S. midterm elections on November 3, then the Friday jobs report (payrolls survey 62k, unemployment 4.2%), ISM manufacturing and services, JOLTS, University of Michigan sentiment, Middle East and Ukraine developments, and the OPEC meeting.

The document is a Fixed Income Weekly Update. Its yield curve opportunity pages and loan strategies pages are bank-product listings (pool transactions, flow partnerships, primary-market loan yields) with little market-directional content.
